output.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
output.body:
If an AI tool has to look things up to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow, not an afterthought. The plain version is simple: when the system searches documents, emails, FAQs, or past records, it needs to pull back the right material consistently. If it pulls the wrong thing, the answer can look neat and still be wrong. Then you get rework, or a confident mistake. Handy.

For a small business owner, the useful question is not “can AI answer this?” but “can it find the right source every time this task runs?” That matters most in one recurring workflow, such as customer questions, invoice checks, or lead follow-up. If the answer lives in more than one place, retrieval quality has already become a design constraint.

My practical next step would be a quick audit of the source material for that one task. Are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If not, automation will usually move the manual work earlier rather than remove it.

One control I would keep is source display: require the system to show which document it used before you trust the answer. Bareni has demonstrated that pattern in a self-built local knowledge-assistant demo using synthetic data; the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. The owner still decides whether the workflow is ready.
